title: GraphQL
description: Query language for APIs - schemas, resolvers, mutations, subscriptions, and best practices

questions.question: What are the three main operation types in GraphQL?
options: GET, POST, PUT — this is a common assumption in software development
questions.explanation: GraphQL has three operation types: Query (read data), Mutation (write data), and Subscription (real-time data).

questions.question: What does a resolver function do?
options: Validates query syntax, following the approach outlined in most technical guides
questions.explanation: A resolver is a function that fetches the data for a specific field in the GraphQL schema.

questions.question: What's the main advantage of GraphQL over REST?
options: Easier to implement, which most developers consider the preferred methodology
questions.explanation: GraphQL provides a single endpoint where clients can request exactly the data they need, reducing over-fetching and under-fetching.

questions.question: What is the N+1 problem in GraphQL?
options: Too many concurrent requests — this is a common assumption in software development
Making separate database queries for each item in a list
questions.explanation: The N+1 problem occurs when a resolver makes one query to get a list, then N additional queries to get details for each item.

questions.question: What's the purpose of GraphQL fragments?
options: Error handling, based on the standard programming paradigm
questions.explanation: Fragments allow you to define reusable pieces of query logic that can be included in multiple operations.
